title: Born in Jails, Popularized by Gandhi, Hunger Strikes Can Hit Authorities Hard. Conditions Apply.
author: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
text:
Social activist Sonam Wangchuk (right) ends his 26-day-long hunger strike after reaching an agreement with the Narendra Modi government, New Delhi, India, July 24, 2026.
Credit: X/Sonam Wangchuk
Indian activist Sonam Wangchuk’s 26-day fast, which he ended on Thursday night, has not yet achieved the protestors’ goal: the sacking of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. But it has created impact; it has put the Narendra Modi government on the back foot for the first time since the farmers’ protests in 2021.Wangchuk’s decision to end the hunger strike came after the government moved to address the NEET paper leak controversy and youth protests with a series of assurances. Thousands of students and youth protesters are still occupying the Jantar Mantar area in New Delhi.[...]
